page.title: Drive a host from a script
page.description: tinyactors run serves one host over JSON-RPC 2.0 on standard input and output: a script spawns actors, answers their sends and moves the clock.

hero.headline: Drive a host from a script
hero.lede: tinyactors run serves one host over JSON-RPC 2.0 on standard input and output. Your script spawns orders, answers their payment requests and moves a simulated clock.

section.heading: Start a host on your charts
section.p: Start one host with --io-processor payments so tinyactors run routes external payment requests back to your script. Closing standard input stops the host.
section.code: tinyactors run --io-processor payments --system shop order.scxml < requests.jsonl
section.p: This order chart asks payments for a charge, retries after 30 seconds of silence and gives up after three attempts.

section.heading: Answer each send the actor makes
section.p: Send run.* requests to control the host and forwarded methods such as actor.state to query actors. Reply to each effect.send notification with run.send.

example.caption: The first order is paid and shipped; the second gets no answer, and its charge goes out again at 30 seconds.

section.heading: Answer a send before its sender moves on
section.p: Pass "hold": true to run.turn to keep an actor waiting after a send marked "waiting": true. Above, the order stays in paying until your script answers in request 5 and turns in request 6.
Without hold, the sender continues immediately and any reply arrives later as an ordinary event.

section.heading: Move the clock yourself
section.p: Advance the host's simulated clock with run.advanceTime instead of waiting in real time. Request 14 skips 30 seconds forward so the next turn fires the second order's timeout immediately.

claim.statement: A session repeats byte for byte
claim.p: The clock is simulated and Math.random has a fixed seed, so the same requests write the same lines, trace ids included.

section.heading: Generate a client from the schema
section.p: Run tinyactors run --schema to print the JSON Schema for every request, response and notification. You can also download it from the run command's page.

claim.p: It may change in any release until a second client uses it. The schema describes the release you have.
